title: Micro-starter templates: resumable stream ergonomics and cross-SDK retry patterns
creator: Aarav Patel
description: Add a set of compact, opinionated starter templates demonstrating resumable streaming, ergonomic abort/retry behavior, and idempotent CLI patterns across TypeScript, Python, and Go. Templates include: Next.js server-streaming component example, FastAPI streaming endpoint + background persister, Go HTTP server that drains/gently shuts down while exporting resume tokens, and minimal CLI examples (py/ts/go) showing resume tokens and retry idempotency. Goal is to reduce onboarding friction and establish canonical patterns for production apps using Redwood SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Four runnable example projects (nextjs, fastapi, go-http, cli-mono) in the starter template repo with README instructions
Each example demonstrates: resumable stream checkpointing (resume token), clear client retry semantics, and graceful shutdown for server components
SDK helpers (RetryPolicy, StreamCheckpoint, ResumeToken helper) implemented in each language with consistent names and minimal surface area
End-to-end walkthrough documented in console docs and linked from SDK quickstarts
Smoke tests exist that simulate network interruption and verify resume behavior for each example
design_notes: We want a minimal abstraction that maps cleanly to each language's async model: AsyncIterator for JS/TS, async generator + asyncio for Python, and channels/context for Go. Tradeoffs: keep SDK surface tiny (helper functions) vs. adding heavy orchestration layer; decision: provide helpers and clear patterns, not a full state store. Resume tokens are opaque strings produced by the server runtime (KV snapshot pointer), stored by the client. We recommend storing tokens in a lightweight user-state store (local file for CLI demo, browser localStorage for Next.js demo, SQLite for FastAPI background persister).
api_surface: RetryPolicy(maxAttempts: number, baseBackoffMs: number, jitter: boolean) -> serializable config
sdk.start_stream({model, prompt, resumeToken?, onMessage?}) -> { iterator, resumeToken } (py/ts/go flavors)
GracefulServer.Drain(ctx) -> ensures in-flight streams finish or expose resume tokens

Write README and step-by-step tutorial in docs, link to console quickstart (Docs)

tests: Unit tests for RetryPolicy backoff schedule and jitter behavior
Integration test: start server, start client streaming, kill connection mid-stream, restart client using saved resume token and verify message sequence continuity
End-to-end CI job that runs all examples in Docker with ephemeral ports and asserts exit codes
Manual UX test: Next.js page reconnects without full re-render and app preserves partial UI state

2026-03-12 Aarav Patel: Added FastAPI background persister plan. Use sqlite for examples; production guidance will recommend K/V store or object store. Note: consider security implications of resume tokens — they may grant stream continuation and should be treated as bearer tokens.

2026-03-13 Priya Kumar: Go server demo implemented. Using context.WithCancel for graceful shutdown and writing resume tokens to JSON file for the demo CLI. Observed a race where token isn't flushed on SIGTERM — adding forced flush in Drain() implementation.
